attrs.evidence: The missing object between a claim and its evidence. R5 had `Claim -> evidence_kind` and let one global table decide whether that kind could discharge that claim; what a global table cannot say is WHY this particular support establishes this particular proposition. Seven argument records exist, at exactly the places where consumption is conditional. `remaining_trust` is mandatory and is the field that earns the object: ARG-LED-C9-MEDIATED-SURFACE names its own source-scan brittleness, ARG-FED-PAIRWISE-CITATION names an inference of this project's that the cited theorem does not make, and ARG-FED-Q2-BOUNDED-CITATION names that no witness is built for s > 3. An argument claiming to close everything would be the thing to distrust.
attrs.prior_art: OMG Structured Assurance Case Metamodel (SACM) 2.3 separates claims, arguments/reasoning, evidence, context and assumptions. GPT-5.6 identified it as the prior art R5 had independently rediscovered. Deliberately NOT imported: seven fields, not a metamodel, and interoperability is not a goal yet.
attrs.review_focus: Argument records are required only where the consumption table says `conditional`. That threshold is a guess. The strongest attack is that a deductive_proof discharging universal_affirmation outright — 20-odd records in this ledger — is exactly where an argument object would earn the most, and none of them has one.
attrs.statement: Nontrivial evidence consumption is mediated by an explicit argument record linking evidence, premise claims and assumptions to the exact obligation of the conclusion, and every argument states its remaining trust.
